title: The Day Boston Was Flooded By 2 Million Gallons Of Syrup
sources: Stephen Puleo (2003), 'Dark Tide: The Great Boston Molasses Flood of 1919'
Smithsonian Magazine (2019), 'The Science of the Great Molasses Flood'
Boston Public Library Archives, 1919 Molasses Disaster

lines.text: In 1919, Boston was hit by a disaster that sounds completely made up.
lines.caps: In 1919, | Boston was hit | by a disaster that | sounds made up.

lines.text: A giant steel tank holding over two million gallons of molasses suddenly exploded.
It unleashed a twenty-five-foot tidal wave of thick brown syrup
racing through city streets at thirty-five miles per hour!
The sticky tsunami destroyed buildings and lifted a train right off its tracks,
trapping terrified pedestrians in warm gooey syrup.
Rescue workers had to wade through waist-deep molasses,
and millions of gallons of saltwater were pumped just to scrub the streets.
For decades afterward, locals swore that on hot summer days,
the entire city of Boston still smelled like sweet molasses!
